q-35725.problem: Given that ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1-18{x}^{2}}{12p{x}^{2}-3x+9}=-2,$  what is the value of $p?$
q-35725.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1-18{x}^{2}}{12p{x}^{2}-3x+9} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{18{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{12p{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{3x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{9}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-18)}{(12p-\frac{3}{x}+\frac{9}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{0-18}{12p-0+0} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2p} & =-2 \\ 4p & =3 \\ p & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-48925.name: Question 3
q-48925.worked_solution:
For sufficiently large negative values of $x,$ we have $|6x-4|=-(6x-4)=-6x+4.$ Consequently, for $x\to -\infty ,$ we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{|6x-4|}{3x+4}={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-6x+4}{3x+4}.
$$

First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{1}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-6x+4}{3x+4} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(\frac{-6x}{x}+\frac{4}{x})}{(\frac{3x}{x}+\frac{4}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(-6+\frac{4}{x})}{(3+\frac{4}{x})} \\  & =\frac{-6+0}{3+0} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

q-78013.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{4{x}^{2}+5}{2x}.$
q-78013.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{4{x}^{2}+5}{2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{4{x}^{2}}{x}+\frac{5}{x})}{(\frac{2x}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(4x+\frac{5}{x})}{2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(4x+0)}{2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }2x \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
